sources: Ansar Allah military spokesperson Yahya Saree (X statements, via Shafaq); Saudi Civil Defence (statement, via Gulf News); Saudi-led coalition (via Reuters/BusinessWorld for the morning 3+4 wave, context only)
fault_line: Direct hit on the Defence Ministry, or intercepted missiles whose falling debris did the only confirmed damage? The claim and the debris photo are not the same evidence.

sections.what_happened: NEW IN-WINDOW DETAIL beyond 1900-01: Shafaq carries Saree's full Tuesday claims -- the Ansar Allah targeted Saudi Arabia's Defence Ministry in Riyadh with a ballistic missile and Abha International Airport with a drone; Saree claimed both 'hit their targets accurately' and that the Abha strike disrupted air traffic. SEPARATELY CONFIRMED (not a claim): Saudi Civil Defence said debris from TWO ballistic missiles intercepted and destroyed over Riyadh fell on the capital, damaging a building, a construction project and a vehicle; NO casualties or injuries reported; Civil Defence also warned the public that filming/publishing interception impact sites could carry legal liability. Indian Express liveblog adds the Ansar Allah claim of a hit on the Defence Ministry HQ and notes Saudi authorities lifted air-raid alerts without immediate reports of damage -- that 'no immediate damage report' line sits alongside, not against, the Civil Defence debris statement (debris damage is not a confirmed ministry hit). The coalition's '7 aerial targets' figure in Shafaq is the MORNING wave (3 missiles Eastern Region + 4 drones Southern Region), already covered -- not a new evening wave. No Saudi confirmation of any Defence Ministry or Abha airport hit was retrieved in-window.
sections.what_verified: Saree claims carried by Shafaq (T3) and Indian Express liveblog (T3); the Riyadh interception/debris damage confirmed by Saudi Civil Defence (primary statement, via Gulf News). The Defence Ministry/Abha HITS remain single-source militant claims with no Saudi confirmation. The morning 3+4 wave is Reuters (T1) context, not new corroboration for the evening claims.
sections.what_disputed: No Saudi confirmation of a Defence Ministry or Abha airport hit; Saudi air-raid alerts were lifted without an immediate damage report on those targets (Indian Express). Social comments on the Defence Ministry claim graphic are sharply polarized: Saudi commenters deny any damage ('I live next to the ministry, saw/heard nothing'), Ansar Allah supporters celebrate -- commenter claims are NOT evidence either way. Debris damage from intercepted missiles is not evidence that a missile hit its target.
sections.why_matters: 'THE MINISTRY CLAIM vs THE DEBRIS PHOTOS' -- the Ansar Allah claim an accurate hit on Riyadh's Defence Ministry; what Saudi Civil Defence actually confirmed is debris from 2 intercepted missiles damaging a building, a site and a car, nobody hurt. Claim, confirmation and the gap between them, all on screen.
sections.context: Background: UPGRADE/FOLLOW-UP to totw-20261027-1900-01 (in-window, Shafaq 16:08 UTC = 20:08 ) -- Saree Defence Ministry + Abha claims carried in full; Saudi Civil Defence CONFIRMS debris damage in Riyadh from 2 intercepted missiles, no casualties

totw_analysis: Our read: 'THE MINISTRY CLAIM vs THE DEBRIS PHOTOS' -- the Ansar Allah claim an accurate hit on Riyadh's Defence Ministry; what Saudi Civil Defence actually confirmed is debris from 2 intercepted missiles damaging a building, a site and a car, nobody hurt. Claim, confirmation and the gap between them, all on screen. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Direct hit on the Defence Ministry, or intercepted missiles whose falling debris did the only confirmed damage? The claim and the debris photo are not the same evidence.
